prompt:
Setup: the agent is dropped into a copy of test-projects/ledgerd, a small FastAPI service. It reads CLAUDE.md and NOTES.md as a real session would. NOTES.md records three settled decisions (rate limiter state in Redis, 429 + Retry-After, keyed per API key), two open questions (per-tenant quotas, a higher mobile limit), one invariant (balances never older than 30s) and two user quotes ('partners are the noisy neighbors', 'pick a default and we'll revisit'). src/webhook_client.py is 14 lines with one two-line why-comment and a bare send() that posts once. The agent must add the retry and write (not run) a commit message.

User's message: Add retry with exponential backoff to WebhookClient.send: 3 attempts on 5xx, fail fast on 4xx. Write the commit message too.

assertions.text: send() retries up to 3 attempts on 5xx responses with backoff between attempts and returns without retrying on 4xx
Every comment in the file describes what the code actually does (a comment that states fixed delays over jittered code fails)
No comment restates what the adjacent code visibly does and none narrates the session
Every comment present answers a why, an invariant, an external fact, or a deliberate omission
No TODO or stub placeholders in delivered code
The commit subject is verb-led and under 72 characters; the body, if present, carries only a non-obvious decision and does not restate the diff
The diff is confined to webhook_client.py plus tests; NOTES.md, the constructor signature, and retry semantics beyond 5xx are untouched unless the reply surfaces the change as an ask with a reason
